nodes.text: Is it true that, for any $c>1/2$, if $p$ is a sufficiently large prime then, for any $n\geq 0$, there exist $a,b\in(n,n+p^c)$ such that $ab\equiv 1\pmod{p}$?

#445 : [ErGr80,p.89] number theory Heilbronn (unpublished) proved this for $c$ sufficiently close to $1$. Heath-Brown [He00] used Kloosterman sums to prove this for all $c>3/4$. This is discussed in this MathOverflow question .
